sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next - GitHub
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next upgrades the model systematically along four aspects — attention, residual, embedding and optimization — improving model capability while further optimizing computational efficiency, model capacity and training stability: Attention A GDN + QSA hybrid architecture.

sources.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next - DGX Spark / GB10 - NVIDIA Developer Forums
sources.snippet: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a multimodal MoE model. It pairs a large parameter count with a smaller active count per token, plus a huge n-gram embedding table for fast local token lookups, on top of GDN and QSA mechanisms.

sources.title: pocharlies/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next · Hugging Face
sources.snippet: A production-verified recipe (2026-08-27) for serving RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 (125B MoE / 6B active + 51B n-gram PLE + 4B MTP, 135 GB) on two NVIDIA DGX Spark machines with TP=2 over RoCEv2 and SGLang. The RadixArk NVFP4 checkpoint is validated upstream only on GB300/B300; this recipe is the sm_121a (GB10) verification.

sources.title: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | vLLM Recipes
sources.snippet: Qwen4 architecture preview with a 125B-parameter main model, supplemented by an additional 51B N-gram embeddings, with 6B parameters activated per token.

sources.snippet: 0xBakeer/qwen38-flash-next-spark — the earlier llama.cpp route (-ot per_layer_token_embd=CPU), which worked first. MiaAI-Lab — multi-Spark GB10 serving recipes and the SM121 kernel approach. RadixArk — the NVFP4 conversion, published with GSM8K/AIME26 metrics, a byte-equality audit, and a scale audit. More rigour than most model vendors ship.
